title: Smoking
description: Lifetime and current cigarette smoking, from questionnaire Section B, Smoking.

smk_ever.title: Smoked at least 100 cigarettes in lifetime
smk_ever.$comment: Source coding: 1=Yes; 2=No; -7 Refused; -9 Don't know. Questionnaire B1: 'Have you smoked at least 100 cigarettes in your entire life?' The data steward says a refused or don't-know answer was routed like No (D017).

smk_status.title: Current smoking status
smk_status.$comment: Source coding: 1=Current; 2=Former; -6 Not applicable; -9 Don't know. Questionnaire B2 offers 'Yes, I smoke now' [1] and 'No, I have quit' [2]. People whose smk_ever is 2, -7 or -9 hold -6 here (D017).
smk_status.x-universe: People who have smoked at least 100 cigarettes in their life (smk_ever = 1)

cigs_day.title: Cigarettes per day (current smokers)
cigs_day.description: Counts above 60 were capped at 60 in the 2024 cleaning, so 60 means 60 or more; a current smoker always has at least 1.
cigs_day.$comment: Source coding: integer 0-99 in the dictionary, (1-60) in questionnaire B3; -6 Not applicable; -9 Don't know. Notes: Current smokers only. The data steward settled the range at 1-60 (D016): the 2024 cleaning capped counts at 60 and the dictionary range was never updated. People whose smk_ever is 2, -7 or -9, and people whose smk_status is 2 or -9, hold -6 here (D017, D029).

smk_age_start.title: Age started smoking (years)
smk_age_start.description: Questionnaire B4 asks: 'How old were you when you started smoking regularly?' Ages below 10 were recoded to -9 (don't know) in the 2024 cleaning.
smk_age_start.$comment: Source coding: integer 5-80 in the dictionary; -6 Not applicable; -9 Don't know. The data steward says real values run 10 to 80, because ages below 10 were recoded to -9 as implausible (D028). The dictionary label does not say 'regularly'; the questionnaire question does.
smk_age_start.x-universe: People who have smoked at least 100 cigarettes in their life (smk_ever = 1)
